description.value: The study investigated amygdala–prefrontal functional connectivity during facial expression processing in depressed inpatients and healthy controls, including associations with MAOA allele activity and illness severity.

spans.text: In the present study, functional connectivity of the amygdala with prefrontal areas involved in emotion regulation was investigated during a facial expression processing task in a sample of 34 depressed inpatients and 31 healthy controls.

value: Depressed patients show decreased functional connectivity of the amygdala with prefrontal areas implicated in the regulation of emotion (dACC and DLPFC corresponding to BA 46 and BA 9) during emotion processing compared to healthy subjects.
Healthy as well as depressed carriers of MAOA-H alleles show decreased amygdala–prefrontal connectivity in the same areas.
Reduced amygdala–prefrontal connectivity is associated with a severe and chronic course of disease in depressed patients.

value: The whole-group task effect analysis yielded robust activations of bilateral amygdala, the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, and large clusters in the lateral prefrontal cortex with peak activity in the dorsolateral parts.

spans.text: The whole-group task effect analysis yielded robust activations of bilateral amygdala [left amygdala: k (cluster size)=96 voxels, peak voxel at x=−20, y=−4, z=−20, t (64)=8.6, p corrected <0.001; right amygdala: k =144, x=32, y=−4, z=−20, t (64)=8.4, p corrected <0.001]. In the whole ACC, only the dorsal part was activated on this level of significance [ k =60, x=6, y=8, z=26, t (64)=6.9, p corrected <0.001]. Furthermore, large and highly significant clusters in the lateral prefrontal cortex were observed with peak activity in the dorsolateral parts (left DLPFC: k =3729, x=−42, y=10, z=26, t (64)=13.2, p corrected <0.001; right DLPFC: k =5064, x=40, y=14, z=26, t (64)=15.25, p corrected <0.001; see Supplementary Figure 1, available online).
